prompt: Why must the basket columns be scaled before PCA?
hint: PCA looks for the largest spread.

choices.text: The shares must add up to 1
choices.why: Scaling does not do that.

choices.text: PCA refuses unscaled data
choices.why: It runs; it just answers a different question.

choices.text: The basket would win alone
choices.why: Yes. The largest spread wins, whatever its unit.

choices.text: Scaling makes PCA faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: How much of the variation did the first three components carry, in percent, one decimal place?
Why did the eighth component carry 0.0% of the variation?
hint: What do the six shares add up to?

choices.text: PCA always discards the last component
choices.why: It kept it; it simply had nothing in it.

choices.text: The extras column is all zeros
choices.why: Its mean is 8.7.

choices.text: There were too few customers
choices.why: 1,200 rows is plenty for eight columns.

choices.text: Shares sum to 100; one is redundant
choices.why: Yes. Seven dimensions dressed as eight.

prompt: Each principal component is at a right ___ to all the components before it.
The first component weighs bakery, eggs and dairy and basket size positive, and fruit, vegetables and greens negative. What does it measure?

choices.text: Bakery set against produce
choices.why: Yes. One end buys bread and cheese, the other produce.

choices.text: Fruit against vegetables
choices.why: That is the second component.

choices.text: Nothing that can be read
choices.why: Here it can be read, by luck.

choices.text: How often a customer orders
choices.why: Orders a month weigh only 0.15.

prompt: Another run of PCA returns the first component with every weight's sign flipped. What changed?

choices.text: The customers' order on the axis is now wrong
choices.why: It is mirrored, which is the same order read backwards.

choices.text: Nothing it means
choices.why: Yes. The sign of a component is arbitrary.

choices.text: The data changed between the two runs
choices.why: A flip happens on the same data.

choices.text: The second component became the first
choices.why: The order by variance is the same.

prompt: What does trustworthiness measure on a map?

choices.text: How much of the variation is kept
choices.why: That is PCA's explained variance.

choices.text: How far apart the groups look
choices.why: That was the silhouette column.

choices.text: Whether neighbours stay together
choices.why: Yes. 1 means all of them were.

choices.text: How fast the map was drawn
choices.why: That was the seconds column.

prompt: On a UMAP map, the bakery island sits far from the fruit island. What may you conclude?
hint: What do t-SNE and UMAP preserve?

choices.text: They are the two most different groups
choices.why: Distances between islands mean little on these maps.

choices.text: The fruit customers will never buy bread
choices.why: A map says nothing like that.

choices.text: UMAP was given too many neighbours
choices.why: The settings were the defaults.

choices.text: Little: these maps keep neighbours
choices.why: Yes. Check distances in the data or on PCA.

prompt: t-SNE's silhouette was 0.754 at perplexity 30 and 0.514 at perplexity 5. By how much did it fall? Three decimal places.
UMAP took 14 seconds in `maps.py` and under three for a second fit in the same program. Why?

choices.text: First-run compilation
choices.why: Yes. The first run in a session pays for it.

choices.text: The second fit used fewer customers
choices.why: Same customers.

choices.text: t-SNE warmed the processor up
choices.why: The timing test ran UMAP twice in its own program.

choices.text: The first fit ran on a graphics card
choices.why: Nothing here uses one.

prompt: Why can t-SNE not place a new customer on a map it has drawn?

choices.text: New customers have different columns
choices.why: They have the same eight.

choices.text: It just arranges given rows
choices.why: Yes. So it has no `transform`.

choices.text: It needs the customer's label
choices.why: No method here uses a label.

choices.text: Its perplexity is too low
choices.why: No setting gives it a transform.

prompt: Order the three methods by how they place new rows, from exact to impossible.
hint: The table at the end of the section.

prompt: Why is the PCA step inserted at position 2 of the pipeline?

choices.text: To replace the logistic regression
choices.why: The logistic regression stays, as the last step.

choices.text: Pipelines only accept new steps at position 2
choices.why: Any position works.

choices.text: To see the prepared columns
choices.why: Yes. After `shapes` and `prepare`, before the model.

choices.text: So it runs before the gaps are filled
choices.why: PCA cannot work on gaps; it comes after the filling.

prompt: With 20 components the churn model made R$ 23,384, more than with all 36 columns. Why does the lesson keep all 36?
hint: Noise, and what a weight means.

choices.text: PCA cannot be saved to a file
choices.why: It can, inside the pipeline.

choices.text: The AUC with 20 components was below 0.8
choices.why: It was 0.815.

choices.text: 20 components are slower than 36 columns
choices.why: They are fewer, so faster.

choices.text: The gain is inside the noise, and the weights stop meaning anything
choices.why: Yes. A weight on a component is a weight on a mixture.

prompt: When does PCA earn its place inside a model? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: When the retention team must read the weights
choices.why: PCA makes the weights unreadable.

choices.text: A distance-based model suffering in many columns
choices.why: Yes, the curse of lesson 6.

choices.text: Thousands of pixel columns
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: 36 well-chosen columns and 38,628 rows
choices.why: That is this problem, and the full model stays.

prompt: A product manager wants a map of all subscribers that will be updated every Monday with the week's new sign-ups placed on it, without the old points moving. Which method?

choices.text: PCA or UMAP, fitted once, with `transform`
choices.why: Yes. Both place new rows on the learned map.

choices.text: k-means with k = 2
choices.why: That groups; it does not draw a map.

choices.text: Any method, since maps never move
choices.why: t-SNE maps do.

choices.text: t-SNE, redrawn every Monday
choices.why: Redrawing moves the old points.
